q.en: Why is the goose a better reward than gold?
q.fa: چرا غاز پاداشی بهتر از طلاست؟

model.en: Because gold would end the story. A goose that sticks people together keeps making the same joke in new company, and it is the joke, not the metal, that a princess who never laughs needs. The gift fits the person who receives it.
model.fa: چون طلا داستان را تمام می‌کرد. غازی که آدم‌ها را به هم می‌چسباند همان شوخی را با جمع تازه تکرار می‌کند و شاهزاده‌ای که هرگز نمی‌خندد به همان شوخی نیاز دارد، نه به فلز. هدیه به کسی می‌خورد که آن را می‌گیرد.

q.en: What is the story really saying about the name 'Simpleton'?

model.en: That the name is wrong. The brothers who are called clever keep what they have, and the one who is called simple gives his bread away, which is the only action in the story that produces anything. The tale quietly swaps the two words.
model.fa: اینکه نام اشتباه است. برادرانی که باهوش خوانده می‌شوند داشته‌هایشان را نگه می‌دارند و آن که ساده‌لوح خوانده می‌شود نانش را می‌بخشد، و این تنها کاری در داستان است که چیزی به بار می‌آورد. داستان آرام آرام دو واژه را جابه‌جا می‌کند.

tip.en: Compare the two behaviours, not the two labels.
tip.fa: دو رفتار را مقایسه کن، نه دو برچسب را.

stories.text: A queen sent her daughter to marry a prince in a far kingdom, with a maid and a talking horse called Falada. On the way the maid refused to bring water and made the princess change clothes and horses. She made her swear never to tell anyone, and at the castle the maid was taken for the bride. The real princess was sent to help the goose boy, and she said nothing. The false bride had Falada killed, and his head was nailed over the gate. Every morning the head spoke to the goose girl as she passed, and she cried quietly. The goose boy tried to pull her golden hair, and she called the wind to blow his hat away. The boy complained to the old king, who watched and saw the truth. The king asked her to tell her story, and she said she had sworn not to. He told her to tell it to the iron stove instead, and she did. The king heard every word and brought the truth to the feast. The false bride was sent away, and the goose girl married the prince.

q.en: Why does the princess keep her oath when breaking it would help?

model.en: Because the oath is the last thing she owns. Her clothes, her horse and her name are gone, and her word is what is left. The story finds a way for her to keep it and still be heard, which is the clever part: the stove is not a person.
model.fa: چون قسم آخرین چیزی است که دارد. لباس، اسب و نامش رفته و  تنها چیزی که مانده حرفش است. داستان راهی پیدا می‌کند که هم قسمش را نگه دارد و هم شنیده شود، و بخش هوشمندانه همین است: تنور آدم نیست.

model.en: She is both, and the story shows the difference between wanting more and taking it. A servant with no future is not a monster; but she takes another woman's name by force and threatens her with death, and the ending is about that threat, not about her ambition.
model.fa: هر دو، و داستان تفاوت «بیشتر خواستن» و «گرفتن» را نشان می‌دهد. خدمتکاری بی‌آینده هیولا نیست؛ اما نام زن دیگری را به زور می‌گیرد و او را به مرگ تهدید می‌کند، و پایان داستان دربارهٔ همین تهدید است، نه جاه‌طلبی او.

stories.text: A little tailor sat sewing by his window and spread jam on his bread. Seven flies came to the jam, and he killed them all with one blow of a cloth. He made a belt that said "Seven at one blow" and went out to see the world. A giant read the belt and thought the little man had killed seven men. The giant squeezed a stone until water ran out; the tailor squeezed a cheese from his coat and water ran out. The giant threw a stone high in the air; the tailor threw a bird, which flew away and never came down. At night the giant tried to kill him in his bed, but the tailor slept in a corner. In the morning he walked out alive, and the other giants ran away. The king read the belt and gave him a place in the army, but the soldiers were afraid of him. So the king promised him half the kingdom and his daughter if he killed two giants in the forest. The tailor climbed a tree, dropped stones on the giants and made them fight each other. He married the princess and became king.

q.en: Is the tailor brave or just lucky?
q.fa: خیاط شجاع است یا فقط خوش‌شانس؟

model.en: He is neither, exactly: he is quick. Every danger is solved by noticing what the other person expects and giving them something else. A cheese for a stone, a bird for a stone, a corner instead of a bed. That is a kind of courage, but it is mostly invention.
model.fa: دقیقاً هیچ‌کدام نیست: او چابک‌است. هر خطر با فهمیدن انتظار طرف مقابل و دادن چیز دیگری حل می‌شود. پنیر به‌جای سنگ، پرنده به‌جای سنگ، گوشه به‌جای تخت. این نوعی شجاعت است، اما بیشتر ابتکار است.

q.en: What does the belt really change?

model.en: Not his strength; only what people believe about him. He kills four giants without a weapon because each one has already decided who he is. The story is about a sentence being stronger than a sword.
model.fa: نه نیروی او؛ فقط باور آدم‌ها را. او چهار غول را بی‌سلاح می‌کشد چون هر کدام از قبل تصمیم گرفته‌اند او کیست. داستان دربارهٔ جمله‌ای است که از شمشیر قوی‌تر است.

tip.en: Say what others believe, then what that belief lets him do.
tip.fa: بگو دیگران چه باور می‌کنند، بعد آن باور چه اجازه‌ای به او می‌دهد.

stories.text: A woman wanted a child, so she asked an old witch for help. The witch gave her a seed, and from the flower came a tiny girl as small as a thumb. The woman called her Thumbelina and made her a bed from a walnut shell. One night a toad carried her away to a lily pad on a stream, because she wanted her for her son. The fish bit through the stem, and the leaf floated away with Thumbelina on it. A beetle carried her into a tree, but the other beetles said she was not pretty, so he put her on a daisy. She lived alone all summer and drank water from the flowers. When winter came she was cold, so she asked a field mouse for help. The mouse let her stay if she kept the home and sang, and Thumbelina agreed. The mouse's friend, a mole, wanted to marry her, and she did not want to live under the ground. In spring she found a swallow that she had helped, and it flew her away to a warm country. There she met a tiny man her own size, and they lived together among the flowers.

q.en: Why is every animal's home wrong for her?
q.fa: چرا خانهٔ هر جانوری برای او نادرست است؟

model.en: Because each home belongs to a different size and a different element: water for the toad, air for the beetle, earth for the mole. She is offered a place in each and none fits. The story is about a girl who has to keep refusing until the last offer is her own size.
model.fa: چون هر خانه به اندازه و عنصری دیگر تعلق دارد: آب برای وزغ، هوا برای سوسک، خاک برای خال‌موش. در هر کدام جایی به او پیشنهاد می‌شود و هیچ‌کدام نمی‌سازد. داستان دربارهٔ دختری است که باید «نه» بگوید تا آخرین پیشنهاد هم‌اندازهٔ خودش باشد.

tip.en: Group the offers by where they are, then say what none of them has.

q.en: What does the swallow represent in the story?

model.en: The one kindness she gave for nothing. She helps the swallow before she needs anything, and the swallow returns years later when she has no other way out. Every escape in this story comes from a small act of care.
model.fa: تنها مهربانی‌ای که بی‌چشمداشت کرد. پیش از آنکه چیزی لازم داشته باشد به پرستو کمک می‌کند و پرستو سال‌ها بعد برمی‌گردد وقتی راه دیگری ندارد. هر رهایی در این داستان از یک کار کوچک مهربانانه می‌آید.

tip.en: Point at the help she gives before she needs any.
tip.fa: به کمکی اشاره کن که پیش از نیازش کرده است.

pairs.en: The king said the prince would find a wife at a royal ball.

pairs.en: The stepsisters wanted new gowns, and Cinderella had to sew them.
pairs.fa: خواهران ناتنی لباس تازه می‌خواستند و سیندرلا باید می‌دوختشان.

pairs.en: "May I go to the ball?" she asked, and the stepmother said she had too much to do.
pairs.fa: پرسید: «می‌توانم به مهمانی بیایم؟» و نامادری گفت کارش زیاد است.

pairs.en: When they left, Cinderella sat by the fireplace and cried.

pairs.en: A fairy godmother came and turned a pumpkin into a coach and mice into horses.

pairs.en: Her old clothes became a gown, and she had glass slippers on her feet.

pairs.fa: با شاهزاده ازدواج کرد و هنوز با خواهران ناتنی‌اش مهربان بود.

stories.text: A kind man lived in a big house with his daughter, and his wife had died. He married a proud woman who had two daughters of her own. The stepmother loved only her daughters and gave the girl the cold attic. She worked in the kitchen and slept by the fireplace, so they called her Cinderella. She was kind to the mice and the birds, and they loved her. The king said the prince would find a wife at a royal ball. The stepsisters wanted new gowns, and Cinderella had to sew them. "May I go to the ball?" she asked, and the stepmother said she had too much to do. When they left, Cinderella sat by the fireplace and cried. A fairy godmother came and turned a pumpkin into a coach and mice into horses. Her old clothes became a gown, and she had glass slippers on her feet. "You must come home before midnight," said the godmother. The prince danced with her all night, and nobody knew who she was. At midnight she ran, and one glass slipper fell on the stairs. The prince said he would marry the girl the slipper fitted, and it fitted Cinderella. She married the prince, and she was still kind to her stepsisters.

q.en: Why does the story make her kind rather than clever?
q.fa: چرا داستان او را مهربان می‌کند، نه زیرک؟

model.en: Because kindness is what she can keep. She loses her father, her room and her name, and the one thing nobody can take is how she treats the mice, the birds and later her stepsisters. The magic is a gift, but the kindness is hers.
model.fa: چون مهربانی تنها چیزی است که می‌تواند نگه دارد. پدر، اتاق و نامش را از دست می‌دهد و تنها چیزی که کسی نمی‌تواند بگیرد رفتارش با موش‌ها، پرنده‌ها و بعد خواهران ناتنی است. جادو هدیه است، اما مهربانی از خودش است.

tip.en: Say what she loses, then what she keeps.
tip.fa: بگو چه از دست می‌دهد، بعد چه نگه می‌دارد.

q.en: Does the glass slipper prove anything real?
q.fa: آیا کفش شیشه‌ای چیز واقعی را ثابت می‌کند؟

model.en: No, and that is the joke. A shoe proves only the size of a foot, not who a person is. The story uses it because the prince has nothing else to go on: he never asked her name, so an object has to do the work of a memory.
model.fa: نه، و همین نکتهٔ خنده‌دار است. کفش فقط اندازهٔ پا را ثابت می‌کند، نه هویت کسی را. داستان از آن استفاده می‌کند چون شاهزاده چیز دیگری ندارد: هرگز نامش را نپرسید، پس یک شیء باید کار حافظه را بکند.

tip.en: Say what the object can and cannot show.
tip.fa: بگو آن شیء چه را می‌تواند و چه را نمی‌تواند نشان دهد.

pairs.fa: هیزم‌شکنی فقیر با دو فرزندش و همسر دومش در حاشیهٔ جنگلی زندگی می‌کرد.

pairs.en: There was little food, and the stepmother said the children should be left in the forest.
pairs.fa: غذا کم بود و نامادری گفت بچه‌ها را باید در جنگل گذاشت.

pairs.en: Hansel heard her, so he filled his pockets with white pebbles from the path.
pairs.fa: هانزل حرفش را شنید، پس جیب‌هایش را از سنگ‌ریزه‌های سفید کنار راه پر کرد.

pairs.en: The children followed their father into the trees, dropping pebbles behind them.
pairs.fa: بچه‌ها دنبال پدرشان به میان درختان رفتند و پشت سرشان سنگ‌ریزه می‌ریختند.

pairs.en: When night came they followed the pebbles home, and their father was glad to see them.
pairs.fa: شب که شد سنگ‌ریزه‌ها را دنبال کردند و به خانه رسیدند و پدرشان از دیدنشان خوشحال شد.

pairs.en: The next time there were no pebbles, so Hansel used bread crumbs, and the birds ate them.
pairs.fa: بار بعد سنگ‌ریزه‌ای نبود، پس هانزل از خرده‌های نان استفاده کرد و پرنده‌ها خوردندشان.

pairs.en: They walked for three days and could not find the way home.
pairs.fa: سه روز راه رفتند و راه خانه را پیدا نکردند.

pairs.en: Then they found a house built of bread and cake, with sugar windows.
pairs.fa: آنگاه خانه‌ای یافتند ساخته از نان و کیک، با پنجره‌های شکرین.

pairs.en: An old woman invited them in and gave them a good dinner and two warm beds.
pairs.fa: پیرزنی آن‌ها را به داخل دعوت کرد و شام خوب و دو تخت گرم داد.

pairs.en: But she was a witch, and in the morning she locked Hansel in a cage.

pairs.fa: سرانجام فر را روشن کرد تا او را بپزد و گفت گرتل داخل را ببیند.

pairs.fa: بچه‌ها مروارید و طلا از خانه برداشتند و راه خانه را یافتند.

stories.text: A poor woodcutter lived at the edge of a forest with his two children and his second wife. There was little food, and the stepmother said the children should be left in the forest. Hansel heard her, so he filled his pockets with white pebbles from the path. The children followed their father into the trees, dropping pebbles behind them. When night came they followed the pebbles home, and their father was glad to see them. The next time there were no pebbles, so Hansel used bread crumbs, and the birds ate them. They walked for three days and could not find the way home. Then they found a house built of bread and cake, with sugar windows. An old woman invited them in and gave them a good dinner and two warm beds. But she was a witch, and in the morning she locked Hansel in a cage. She fed him every day to make him fat, and made Gretel do the work. At last she lit the oven to cook him, and told Gretel to look inside. Gretel said she did not understand, so the witch leaned in, and Gretel pushed her into the fire. The children took pearls and gold from the house and found their way home.

q.fa: بار اول چگونه راه بازگشت را یافتند؟

q.en: Who is really responsible for the children being lost?
q.fa: واقعاً چه کسی مسئول گم شدن بچه‌هاست؟

model.en: The stepmother proposes it and the father agrees, so the father carries the blame, because he is the one who walks them into the trees. The story is careful: it is hunger that starts everything, and fear that lets a parent obey.
model.fa: نامادری پیشنهاد می‌دهد و پدر می‌پذیرد، پس تقصیر پدر است، چون اوست که آن‌ها را به میان درختان می‌برد. داستان دقیق است: گرسنگی همه چیز را شروع می‌کند و ترس باعث می‌شود پدری اطاعت کند.

tip.en: Separate who suggests from who acts.
tip.fa: کسی که پیشنهاد می‌دهد را از کسی که عمل می‌کند جدا کن.

q.en: Why is Gretel, not Hansel, the one who ends it?
q.fa: چرا گرتل و نه هانزل کار را تمام می‌کند؟

model.en: Because Hansel is in a cage, and his cleverness was used up on the way there. Gretel has been doing the witch's work for weeks, so she knows the oven and the kitchen, and she wins by pretending to be helpless, which is exactly what the witch expects of her.
model.fa: چون هانزل در قفس است و زیرکی‌اش در راه مصرف شده. گرتل هفته‌ها کار جادوگر را کرده، پس فر و آشپزخانه را می‌شناسد، و با تظاهر به ناتوانی برنده می‌شود، همان چیزی که جادوگر از او انتظار دارد.

tip.en: Point at what she has learned while he was locked up.
tip.fa: به چیزی اشاره کن که او هنگام زندانی بودن برادرش یاد گرفته.

blurb.en: A queen asks her mirror a question every morning, and the answer finally turns against her.
blurb.fa: ملکه هر صبح از آینه‌اش سؤالی می‌پرسد و سرانجام پاسخ به زیان خودش می‌شود.

pairs.en: A king and queen had a daughter with white skin, red lips and black hair, and they called her Snow White.
pairs.fa: پادشاه و ملکه‌ای دختری با پوست سفید، لب سرخ و موی سیاه داشتند و او را سفیدبرفی نامیدند.

pairs.en: Her mother died, and the king married a beautiful queen who had a magic mirror.
pairs.fa: مادرش مرد و پادشاه با ملکه‌ای زیبا ازدواج کرد که آینه‌ای جادویی داشت.

pairs.en: Every morning the queen asked, "Mirror, who is the fairest in the land?"
pairs.fa: هر صبح ملکه می‌پرسید: «آینه، چه کسی زیباترین سرزمین است؟»

pairs.en: One morning the mirror said Snow White was the fairest now.
pairs.fa: یک صبح آینه گفت حالا سفیدبرفی زیباترین است.

pairs.en: The queen told a huntsman to take Snow White into the forest and kill her.
pairs.fa: ملکه به شکارچی گفت سفیدبرفی را به جنگل ببرد و بکشد.

pairs.en: He could not do it, so he told her to run and never come back, and he carried a deer's heart to the queen.
pairs.fa: نتوانست این کار را بکند، پس گفت بدو و هرگز برنگرد، و قلب آهویی را برای ملکه برد.

pairs.en: Snow White found a small cottage with seven small plates and seven small beds.
pairs.fa: سفیدبرفی کلبه‌ای کوچک با هفت بشقاب و هفت تخت کوچک پیدا کرد.

pairs.en: Seven dwarfs came home from the mine and let her stay to keep house.
pairs.fa: هفت کوتوله از معدن به خانه آمدند و گذاشتند بماند و خانه‌داری کند.

pairs.en: "Never open the door to a stranger," they warned.
pairs.fa: هشدار دادند: «هرگز در را به روی غریبه باز نکن.»

pairs.en: The queen came as an old woman with tight laces, and Snow White fell to the floor.
pairs.fa: ملکه در هیئت پیرزنی با بندهای تنگ آمد و سفیدبرفی روی زمین افتاد.

pairs.en: The dwarfs cut the laces, and she could breathe again.
pairs.fa: کوتوله‌ها بندها را بریدند و او دوباره نفس کشید.

pairs.en: Then the queen brought a poisoned comb, and again the dwarfs saved her.
pairs.fa: بعد ملکه شانه‌ای زهرآلود آورد و باز کوتوله‌ها نجاتش دادند.

pairs.en: At last she offered a poisoned apple, and Snow White bit it and fell.
pairs.fa: سرانجام سیبی زهرآلود تعارف کرد و سفیدبرفی گاز زد و افتاد.

pairs.en: The dwarfs put her in a glass coffin on a hill, where a prince found her.
pairs.fa: کوتوله‌ها او را در تابوتی شیشه‌ای روی تپه‌ای گذاشتند و شاهزاده‌ای آنجا پیدایش کرد.

pairs.en: The apple fell from her mouth when he kissed her, and she woke and married him.
pairs.fa: وقتی بوسیدش سیب از دهانش افتاد و بیدار شد و با او ازدواج کرد.

stories.text: A king and queen had a daughter with white skin, red lips and black hair, and they called her Snow White. Her mother died, and the king married a beautiful queen who had a magic mirror. Every morning the queen asked, "Mirror, who is the fairest in the land?" One morning the mirror said Snow White was the fairest now. The queen told a huntsman to take Snow White into the forest and kill her. He could not do it, so he told her to run and never come back, and he carried a deer's heart to the queen. Snow White found a small cottage with seven small plates and seven small beds. Seven dwarfs came home from the mine and let her stay to keep house. "Never open the door to a stranger," they warned. The queen came as an old woman with tight laces, and Snow White fell to the floor. The dwarfs cut the laces, and she could breathe again. Then the queen brought a poisoned comb, and again the dwarfs saved her. At last she offered a poisoned apple, and Snow White bit it and fell. The dwarfs put her in a glass coffin on a hill, where a prince found her. The apple fell from her mouth when he kissed her, and she woke and married him.

expressions.exampleFa: روی زمین افتاد و نتوانست حرکت کند.

note.fa: «could not» می‌گوید کار برای او ناممکن بود، به دلیلی درون خودش، نه بیرون.

grammar.example: At last the queen offered an apple.

note.en: 'At last' marks the final attempt after several failures.
note.fa: «at last» آخرین تلاش پس از چند شکست را نشان می‌دهد.

q.en: What does the queen ask the mirror?
q.fa: ملکه از آینه چه می‌پرسد؟

why.en: Her question is about beauty, every morning.
why.fa: پرسش او هر صبح دربارهٔ زیبایی است.

q.en: What does the huntsman bring the queen?
q.fa: شکارچی چه چیزی برای ملکه می‌برد؟

why.en: He kills a deer instead of the girl.
why.fa: به‌جای دختر آهویی می‌کشد.

q.en: Where does Snow White live in the forest?
q.fa: سفیدبرفی در جنگل کجا زندگی می‌کند؟

options: In a small cottage with seven dwarfs

why.en: The cottage has seven plates and seven beds.
why.fa: کلبه هفت بشقاب و هفت تخت دارد.

q.en: Which trick finally works?
q.fa: کدام نیرنگ سرانجام کار می‌کند؟

why.en: The apple is the third and the only one that stops her.
why.fa: سیب سومین و تنها موردی است که او را از کار می‌اندازد.

q.en: How does she wake up?
q.fa: چگونه بیدار می‌شود؟

options: A prince kisses her and the apple falls out

why.en: The piece of apple leaves her mouth when he kisses her.
why.fa: با بوسهٔ او تکهٔ سیب از دهانش بیرون می‌آید.

q.en: The dwarfs told her to open the door to nobody.
q.fa: کوتوله‌ها گفتند در را به روی هیچ‌کس باز نکند.

why.en: They warned her three times.
why.fa: سه بار هشدار دادند.

q.en: The queen made only one attempt on Snow White's life.
q.fa: ملکه فقط یک بار به جان سفیدبرفی سوءقصد کرد.

why.en: Laces, comb and apple: three attempts after the huntsman.
why.fa: بند، شانه و سیب: سه تلاش پس از شکارچی.

q.en: Snow White looked dead but did not change.
q.fa: سفیدبرفی مرده به نظر می‌رسید اما تغییر نمی‌کرد.

why.en: The dwarfs kept her because she still looked asleep.
why.fa: کوتوله‌ها نگهش داشتند چون هنوز خوابیده به نظر می‌رسید.

blanks.sentence: The queen asked, "Mirror, who is the ___ in the land?"
Seven ___ came home from the mine.
They put her in a glass ___.

hint.en: The box for a dead person.

q.en: Why does the mirror matter more than the queen's beauty?
q.fa: چرا آینه از زیبایی ملکه مهم‌تر است؟

model.en: Because the queen does not trust her own eyes. A mirror answer is the only proof she accepts, so when it changes its mind she has nothing to fall back on. The story turns a private worry into a public test.
model.fa: چون ملکه به چشم خودش اعتماد ندارد. پاسخ آینه تنها مدرکی است که می‌پذیرد، پس وقتی نظرش عوض می‌شود چیزی برای تکیه ندارد. داستان نگرانی‌ای خصوصی را به آزمونی عمومی تبدیل می‌کند.

tip.en: Say what she needs the mirror for.
tip.fa: بگو او آینه را برای چه می‌خواهد.

q.en: Is Snow White careful or careless?
q.fa: سفیدبرفی محتاط است یا بی‌احتیاط؟

model.en: She is careful at first and careless at the end. The dwarfs warn her three times; she opens the door wider each time, and the third time she believes an old woman who eats half an apple to prove it is safe. Hunger and politeness beat the warning.
model.fa: اول محتاط است و در پایان بی‌احتیاط. کوتوله‌ها سه بار هشدار می‌دهند؛ هر بار در را بیشتر باز می‌کند و بار سوم به پیرزنی باور می‌کند که نصف سیب را می‌خورد تا بی‌خطر بودنش را ثابت کند. گرسنگی و ادب بر هشدار چیره می‌شوند.

tip.en: Compare her first decision with her last one.
tip.fa: اولین تصمیمش را با آخرین تصمیمش مقایسه کن.

blurb.en: A cat asks for boots and turns a miller's youngest son into a marquis, with presents, a river and one very small mouse.
blurb.fa: گربه‌ای چکمه می‌خواهد و پسر کوچک آسیابان را با هدیه، رودخانه و موشکی بسیار کوچک به یک مارکی تبدیل می‌کند.

pairs.en: A miller died and left his three sons his mill, his donkey, and his cat.
pairs.fa: آسیابانی مرد و آسیاب، الاغ و گربه‌اش را برای سه پسرش گذاشت.

pairs.en: The youngest son got the cat and thought it was a poor gift.
pairs.fa: پسر کوچک گربه را گرفت و فکر کرد هدیهٔ بی‌ارزشی است.

pairs.en: "Give me a pair of boots," said the cat, "and I will make you rich."
pairs.fa: گربه گفت: «یک جفت چکمه به من بده و ثروتمندت می‌کنم.»

pairs.en: The cat put on the boots, filled a bag with carrots, and caught rabbits in a field.
pairs.fa: گربه چکمه‌ها را پوشید، کیسه‌ای هویج پر کرد و در کشتزاری خرگوش گرفت.

pairs.en: He took the rabbits to the king and said they were a present from the Marquis of Carabas.
pairs.fa: خرگوش‌ها را نزد پادشاه برد و گفت هدیه‌ای از مارکی دو کاراباست.

pairs.en: The king was pleased, and the presents kept coming.
pairs.fa: پادشاه خشنود شد و هدیه‌ها ادامه یافت.

pairs.en: One day the cat told his master to swim in the river when the king's coach passed.
pairs.fa: روزی گربه به اربابش گفت وقتی کالسکهٔ پادشاه می‌گذرد در رودخانه شنا کند.

pairs.en: The cat shouted that the Marquis was drowning and that thieves had taken his clothes.
pairs.fa: گربه فریاد زد مارکی دارد غرق می‌شود و دزدها لباس‌هایش را برده‌اند.

pairs.en: The king gave him fine clothes, and the princess fell in love with him.
pairs.fa: پادشاه لباس‌های فاخر داد و شاهزاده عاشقش شد.

pairs.en: The cat ran ahead and told the farmers to say the fields belonged to the Marquis.
pairs.fa: گربه جلوتر دوید و به کشاورزان گفت بگویند زمین‌ها مال مارکی است.

pairs.en: When the king asked, they all said yes, so the Marquis seemed very rich.
pairs.fa: وقتی پادشاه پرسید همه بله گفتند، پس مارکی بسیار ثروتمند به نظر می‌رسید.

pairs.en: The cat came to a castle owned by an ogre who could change into any animal.
pairs.fa: گربه به قلعه‌ای رسید که مال غولی بود که می‌توانست به هر جانوری تبدیل شود.

pairs.en: "Can you become a lion?" asked the cat, and the ogre became a lion.
pairs.fa: گربه پرسید: «می‌توانی شیر شوی؟» و غول شیر شد.

pairs.en: "Can you become something very small, like a mouse?"
pairs.fa: «می‌توانی چیزی بسیار کوچک شوی، مثل موش؟»

pairs.en: The ogre became a mouse, and the cat ate him in one bite.
pairs.fa: غول موش شد و گربه او را با یک لقمه خورد.

pairs.en: The Marquis married the princess, and the cat became a great lord.
pairs.fa: مارکی با شاهزاده ازدواج کرد و گربه اربابی بزرگ شد.

stories.text: A miller died and left his three sons his mill, his donkey, and his cat. The youngest son got the cat and thought it was a poor gift. "Give me a pair of boots," said the cat, "and I will make you rich." The cat put on the boots, filled a bag with carrots, and caught rabbits in a field. He took the rabbits to the king and said they were a present from the Marquis of Carabas. The king was pleased, and the presents kept coming. One day the cat told his master to swim in the river when the king's coach passed. The cat shouted that the Marquis was drowning and that thieves had taken his clothes. The king gave him fine clothes, and the princess fell in love with him. The cat ran ahead and told the farmers to say the fields belonged to the Marquis. When the king asked, they all said yes, so the Marquis seemed very rich. The cat came to a castle owned by an ogre who could change into any animal. "Can you become a lion?" asked the cat, and the ogre became a lion. "Can you become something very small, like a mouse?" The ogre became a mouse, and the cat ate him in one bite. The Marquis married the princess, and the cat became a great lord.

model.en: Both, and the story does not mind. He lies to the king, scares farmers into lying and kills the ogre, but every lie is aimed at getting his master out of poverty, and the master never asks how. The tale sides with the clever servant, not with the truth.
model.fa: هر دو، و داستان اهمیتی نمی‌دهد. به پادشاه دروغ می‌گوید، کشاورزان را می‌ترساند تا دروغ بگویند و غول را می‌کشد، اما هر دروغ برای بیرون آوردن اربابش از فقر است و ارباب هرگز نمی‌پرسد چگونه. داستان طرف خدمتکار زیرک است، نه طرف حقیقت.

model.en: Because he listens. The mill and the donkey are already useful, so the older brothers have nothing to learn; the youngest has only a cat, and he does what the cat asks without arguing. The story rewards the person who takes advice, not the one who owns the most.
model.fa: چون گوش می‌دهد. آسیاب و الاغ از قبل به کار می‌آیند، پس برادران بزرگ‌تر چیزی برای یاد گرفتن ندارند؛ کوچک‌ترین فقط گربه‌ای دارد و بی‌بحث کاری را که گربه می‌گوید انجام می‌دهد. داستان کسی را پاداش می‌دهد که نصیحت می‌پذیرد، نه کسی که بیشترین دارایی را دارد.

tip.en: Compare what each son has to do with what he is given.

stories.text: Ali Baba was a poor woodcutter who took his donkeys into the forest every day. One day he saw forty robbers stop at a great rock. The captain said "Open Sesame", and the rock opened onto a cave. When they left, Ali Baba said the words, took some gold and went home. His rich brother Cassim went into the cave and forgot the words when he was inside. The robbers found him there and killed him. Morgiana, the clever servant, hid the death and kept the family out of questions. A robber marked the door with chalk, and she marked every door in the street. The captain came back as an oil merchant with thirty-nine men hidden in jars. Morgiana found the men in the jars and killed them one by one. She danced for the captain and stabbed him. Ali Baba's son married her, and the treasure stayed with the family.

q.en: Why is Morgiana the real hero?
q.fa: چرا مرجانه قهرمان واقعی است؟

model.en: Because she is the only one who looks. Ali Baba finds the cave by accident and Cassim dies of greed, but every danger after that is noticed by a servant: a chalk mark, a jar that breathes, a guest who counts his men. The story gives the cleverness to the person with the least power.
model.fa: چون تنها کسی است که نگاه می‌کند. علی‌بابا تصادفی غار را می‌یابد و قاسم از طمع می‌میرد، اما هر خطر بعدی را خدمتکاری می‌بیند: یک علامت گچ، خمره‌ای که نفس می‌کشد، مهمانی که مردانش را می‌شمارد. داستان زیرکی را به کسی می‌دهد که کمترین قدرت را دارد.

tip.en: List the clues she notices that others miss.
tip.fa: نشانه‌هایی را که او می‌بیند و دیگران نمی‌بینند فهرست کن.

q.en: What does the password really protect?
q.fa: رمز واقعاً از چه چیزی محافظت می‌کند؟

model.en: Nothing much. Two words are enough to open the cave, so the treasure is guarded by secrecy rather than strength, and one man hearing a sentence destroys that. The thieves' real security was that nobody knew the rock was a door.
model.fa: چیز زیادی نه. دو کلمه برای باز کردن غار کافی است، پس گنج با پنهان‌کاری محافظت می‌شود نه با زور، و یک نفر که جمله‌ای را بشنود آن را نابود می‌کند. امنیت واقعی دزدها این بود که کسی نمی‌دانست سنگ یک در است.

tip.en: Say what actually keeps the gold safe, and how thin it is.
tip.fa: بگو واقعاً چه چیزی طلا را ایمن نگه می‌دارد و چقدر شکننده است.

blurb.en: A piece of a broken mirror turns a boy cruel, and a girl walks north to melt it with her tears.

pairs.en: A troll made a mirror that made good things look bad, and it broke in the sky.
pairs.fa: جنّی آینه‌ای ساخت که خوبی‌ها را بد نشان می‌داد و آینه در آسمان شکست.

pairs.fa: تکه‌ای از آن به چشم و قلب کای رفت و او بی‌رحم شد.

pairs.en: He called the roses ugly and went off with a woman in a white sledge: the Snow Queen.
pairs.fa: گل‌های سرخ را زشت خواند و با زنی در سورتمه‌ای سفید رفت: ملکهٔ برفی.

pairs.fa: گردا به جست‌وجویش رفت و رودخانه، پیرزنی و شاهزاده‌ای در راه کمکش کردند.

pairs.en: A robber girl gave her a reindeer and her own mittens.

pairs.fa: او را نمی‌شناخت، چون آینه هنوز در قلبش بود.

pairs.en: Gerda cried, and her tears washed the piece out of his eye.

stories.text: A troll made a mirror that made good things look bad, and it broke in the sky. A piece of it went into Kai's eye and heart, and he became cruel. He called the roses ugly and went off with a woman in a white sledge: the Snow Queen. Gerda went to look for him, and a river, an old woman and a prince helped her on the way. A robber girl gave her a reindeer and her own mittens. The reindeer carried her north to the ice palace. Kai was trying to make a word out of pieces of ice, and he could not. He did not know her, because the mirror was still in his heart. Gerda cried, and her tears washed the piece out of his eye. He cried too, and the glass left his heart. The ice pieces fell into the word eternity, and they went home, and it was summer.

model.en: Because the glass is beaten by warmth, and she is the one person who keeps walking towards him without a reason. A stronger character could not help: the spell has no enemy to fight, only a cold heart to thaw, and patience is the only weapon that works.

stories.text: A king had twelve daughters who slept in one room, and he locked the door himself every night. Every morning their shoes were worn out, and nobody knew why. He promised a prince could marry one of them if he found the secret, and sent away anyone who failed. An old soldier came home with little money and took the task. A woman gave him a cloak that made him invisible and told him not to drink the wine. He pretended to sleep, and the eldest opened a door in the floor. He followed them down to a wood of gold trees and a lake with twelve boats. Twelve princes rowed them across, and they danced until morning. He took a gold cup as proof, and stepped on the youngest one's dress. On the third night he brought the cup to the king. The princesses had to admit the truth, and he married the eldest.

q.en: Why is the locked door useless?
q.fa: چرا درِ قفل‌شده بی‌فایده است؟

model.en: Because the king is guarding the wrong thing. He checks the door every night, and the way out is in the floor, under the bed, in the room he believes is sealed. A lock only works if you know where the opening is.
model.fa: چون پادشاه از چیز اشتباهی نگهبانی می‌کند. هر شب در را بازرسی می‌کند و راه خروج در زمین است، زیر تخت، در همان اتاقی که فکر می‌کند بسته است. قفل فقط وقتی کار می‌کند که بدانی درز کجاست.

model.fa: هر دو. هر شب در یک اتاق قفل می‌شوند، که هر چقدر هم راحت باشد زندان است؛ اما سال‌ها به پدرشان دروغ هم می‌گویند و می‌گذارند مردهای دیگر به‌خاطر شکست رانده شوند. داستان بیشتر از داوری دربارهٔ آن‌ها، نشان می‌دهد اتاق قفل‌شده به آدم‌ها چه یاد می‌دهد.

stories.text: Aladdin was poor, and a magician told him a cave held treasure that only he could open. He went down, took the lamp, and the magician shut him in. He rubbed his hands, and a spirit of the ring took him home. His mother cleaned the lamp, and a spirit appeared and granted wishes. They asked for food, and it came on a silver table. Aladdin asked for gold, fine clothes and a horse, and he went to the palace. The Sultan said he could marry the princess if he sent forty bowls of gold and stones. The lamp answered, and forty men carried them. The magician came back, bought the old lamp for a new one, and took palace and princess away. Aladdin followed with the ring and found them far away. He took the lamp back and asked the spirit to bring everything home. He returned to the palace and lived with the princess.

q.en: Is Aladdin's luck really his?
q.fa: بخت علاءالدین واقعاً از خودش است؟

model.en: No, and the story knows it. He is chosen for a cave he did not find, given a ring he did not ask for, and reminded to keep a lamp only by accident. His one real skill is listening quickly and using what is in his hand.
model.fa: نه، و داستان این را می‌داند. برای غاری انتخاب می‌شود که خودش پیدا نکرده، انگشتری می‌گیرد که نخواسته و فقط تصادفی به یاد می‌آورد چراغ را نگه دارد. تنها مهارت واقعی‌اش زود شنیدن و به کار بردن چیزی است که در دست دارد.

tip.en: List what is given, then find the one thing he does himself.
tip.fa: بگو چه چیزهایی داده شده، بعد تنها کاری که خودش می‌کند را پیدا کن.

q.en: Why does the lamp change hands so easily?
q.fa: چرا چراغ این‌قدر راحت دست‌به‌دست می‌شود؟

model.en: Because its power belongs to whoever holds it, not to whoever deserves it. There is no test and no loyalty; the spirit obeys the object. That is why the story's ending is about getting the lamp back rather than defeating the magician.
model.fa: چون قدرتش از آنِ کسی است که در دستش دارد، نه کسی که سزاوارش است. نه آزمونی هست و نه وفاداری؛ جن از شیء اطاعت می‌کند. به همین دلیل پایان داستان دربارهٔ پس گرفتن چراغ است، نه شکست دادن جادوگر.

tip.en: Say who the power actually obeys.
tip.fa: بگو قدرت واقعاً از چه کسی اطاعت می‌کند.
